physical_harm: Injuries including lacerated wounds over parietal area and left frontal area, and injuries on the body sufficient to cause death
number_of_offences: Number of offences/counts charged: 3 (A-1 to A-3); Number of offences finally upheld: 1 (A-1 under Section 302 IPC)
premeditation_planning: The court found premeditation/planning as the circumstances formed a complete chain pointing to the guilt of the accused
key_evidence_accepted: The time when the deceased was with A-1 and was found dead was so proximate which pointed to the guilt of A-1. A-1 failed to explain the circumstances in which he parted the company of the deceased which was a strong militating circumstance against A-1. The subsequent conduct of A-1 threatening A-4 and PW-7 was also a relevant circumstance. The recovery of the crime weapon at the instance of A-1 was yet another incriminating circumstance in the chain which led to the conclusion pointing to the guilt of A-1.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, particularly PWs 6, 7, and 10, whose evidence established that the victim-deceased was last seen alive in the company of A-1 on the fateful evening. The court also noted that the evidence of PW17 was far from convincing and not of much assistance to the prosecution.
post_offence_conduct: The subsequent conduct of A-1 threatening A-4 and PW-7 was a relevant circumstance indicating his nexus with the offence.

legal_representation.accused: E. R. Sumathy (AC.), Sunil Kumar Jain, Parmatma Jain, Kaushik Chaudhary, Pawanshree Agrawal
legal_representation.state: Chanchal Kumar Ganguli, Kabir Shankar Bose, C Narmada, Saakaar Sardana, Anip Sachthey

investigation_status: Case registered on 12.11.2008, charge sheet filed against three accused, investigation completed

appeal_history.trial_court: Convicted A-1 to A-3 under s.302/120B/34/376(2)(g) IPC and s.25, 27, 35 of the Arms Act; A-4 under s.120B read with s.302 IPC
appeal_history.high_court: Upheld conviction of A-1 under s.302 IPC, set aside conviction under s.376(2)(g) IPC, modified death sentence to life imprisonment; confirmed conviction of A-4 under s.1208 IPC and life imprisonment
appeal_history.supreme_court: Dismissed appeal of A-1, allowed appeals of A-2 to A-4, acquitted A-2 to A-4

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the deceased was last seen alive in the company of A-1, and the time gap between when she was last seen and her death was so small that it pointed to A-1's guilt. The recovery of the crime weapon at A-1's instance and A-1's subsequent threatening behavior were also incriminating circumstances. The prosecution also relied on circumstantial evidence, including call records and the absence of a function at Rajnagar High School.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to establish a complete chain of circumstantial evidence pointing to the guilt of A-2, A-3, and A-4. They contended that the call records and recoveries were insufficient to prove conspiracy or guilt, and that the prosecution did not establish motive or direct involvement of these appellants in the murder.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that in cases of circumstantial evidence, the circumstances must be fully established beyond any reasonable doubt, form a complete chain pointing to the guilt of the accused, and be consistent with the hypothesis of guilt. The court emphasized that mere suspicion is not sufficient for conviction.
precedent_relied_upon: Vivek Kalra vs. State of Rajasthan (2014) 12 SCC 439; State of U.P. vs. Satish (2005) 3 SCC 114; State of Rajasthan vs. Kashi Ram (2006) 12 SCC 254; Geejaganda Somaiah v. State of Karnataka (2007) 9 SCC 315; Swamy Shraddananda @ Murali Manohar Mishra v. State of Karnataka (2007) 12 SCC 288; Gagan Kanojia And Anr. v. State of Punjab (2006) 13 SCC 516; Mohd. Mannan @ Abdul Mannan vs. State of Bihar (2011) 5 SCC 317; Inspector of Police, Tamil Nadu v. John David (2011) 5 SCC 509
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed on A-1 under Section 302 IPC because the prosecution established a complete chain of circumstantial evidence pointing to his guilt. The court found that the circumstances were consistent with the hypothesis of his guilt and that the conviction was supported by the evidence.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The court considered the lack of motive as a mitigating factor, noting that the prosecution did not establish a motive for the murder. However, the court emphasized that the absence of motive does not necessarily exonerate the accused if the circumstantial evidence is strong.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The court considered the proximity of the time when the deceased was with A-1 and when she was found dead as an aggravating factor. The subsequent conduct of A-1, including threatening others, and the recovery of the crime weapon were also aggravating factors.
other_sentence_order: Appellants 2 to 4 (Siddique Mia, Mustaque Mia, and Durga Sutradhar) were acquitted of all the offences and directed to be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other case.
